title: A stuck alert means someone must act: none for an agent whose part is done or a supervisor with nothing to dispatch, and a real one names its task and the one command that acts on it
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the module comment's `agent_stuck`, `observe`, and the observations read: crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs `OBSERVATIONS`), web/src/home.ts (`needsYou`, `alertMoot`, `alertStale`; an item's `command`), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/attention.rs (what the supervisor has to dispatch: `pending`, `told`, the question) and docs/fleet-architecture.md (the alert list's `agent_stuck`; `spawn task restart`).

The problem, measured on the live fleet over the 48 h to 2026-11-11 13:05Z (sync/backlog.md S13). There were 19 `agent_stuck` alerts, and 15 fired on workers whose task had just landed: within seconds of `landing -> landed`, cleared 2.6-12.3 s later on the worker's stop. That is 15 of the 21 landings. The supervisor was "stuck (0.57): WAITING" in Needs you for 3 h while no mission had work open (lead-mac's screenshot sync/home-2026-11-11-2155.png). At most 3 of the 19 were about an agent that needed anyone. The alert step fires on the model judge's `stuck` score alone. An agent whose part is done waits, and a judge reads waiting as stuck. The page can only drop an alert whose session ended or whose score is stale.

Required behaviour.
(a) No `agent_stuck` alert fires, whatever the judge's score, for:
- a worker whose task is reported, gated, landing, landed, held, or waiting for a review (its part is done; what it waits on is the gate, the owner or a reviewer);
- the supervisor while it has nothing to dispatch: no open question to the owner, no pending or told escalation (the attention view's `pending` and `told`), and no mission with an objective open.
An open alert for such an agent clears at the record that made it so, with that record's id as `cleared_evidence.event_id` (for a worker: its task's `task.reported`, `task.gated` and so on).
(b) An agent stuck in its own work still fires one alert, as today. A worker's alert's evidence names its `task` (the task id) and `command`, the one command that acts on it: `spawn task restart --id <task>`. Needs you's item for it carries that command (the item's `command`, shown to copy).
(c) The agent page and the alert say why an agent in (a) is not stuck ("its task is reported, waiting for its gate"; "nothing to dispatch"), so a person reading WAITING knows what it waits on.
(d) docs/fleet-architecture.md's alert list says (a) and (b).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/057.sh. A real `spawn loop` runs with the supervisor on (alert step every 2 s), with `spawn serve`, a fake engine that ends a turn on every prompt, and a fake model judge that scores the sessions it is told to as stuck 0.9, WAITING. Tasks are assigned and reported through `spawn_control_record`, and a turn is provoked by `spawn submit` of a line. Its checks read `GET /api/alerts` and web/src/home.ts's `needsYou` under node:
- (1) The supervisor, with no mission at all, judged stuck after a turn: no `agent_stuck` alert for it.
- (2) A worker whose task is reported, judged stuck after a turn: none.
- (3) A worker whose task is delivered, judged stuck after a turn: one open alert, evidence `task` 2 and `command` "spawn task restart --id 2", and Needs you's item for it carries that command.
- (4) That task is then reported: the alert is cleared within 15 s, `cleared_evidence.event_id` the `task.reported` record.
It fails with 1 on aca25c10: (1) and (2) fire, (3) has no task or command, and (4) stays open.

The product reason. An alert is a claim that a person must act. Today four in five stuck alerts are about an agent that finished its work or has none, and the owner has learned to read "An agent looks stuck" as noise. The one that is real is lost among them.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: alerts.rs unit tests for each state in (a), the supervisor's three conditions, and (b), and a web/test test for the item's command.
